synopsis: Excavators can strike people or trucks with their counterweight or working equipment during swing without travelling; swing contact can be fatal, but separate agency statistics quantifying its frequency or share of serious collisions were not found [f3377, f3579, f3380, f11424]. Rotation therefore needs distinct detection zones and interventions: ISO 21815-4 was under publication in October 2026 and addresses motion inhibition before rotation starts, expressly excluding avoidance through automatic braking [f11428, f11422, f15153]. Komatsu KomVision launched on the PC200-11 in Japan in December 2019, followed by the PC200i-12 in December 2024; it stops at travel or swing start rather than during ongoing swing, and must be disabled during trailer loading because a rapid stop can destabilize the machine [f1640, f1642, f11427]. Virtual evidence remains limited: the 2019 excavator safety algorithm used kinematic working-area prediction and time-to-collision-based modes but had no field comparison, and comprehensive production-scale excavator vehicle-in-the-loop testing was not found [f6204, f6366, f5342]. TERA couples excavator and terrain mechanics and compares track deformation and velocity with a real excavator, but is not an ISO 21815 braking study; virtual swing scenarios still need upper-structure kinematics [f3968, f3969, f4131, f4361]. Available tools include MathWorks R2026b excavator examples, but rendered excavator images retain a significant reality gap, and transferring braking settings between loaders and excavators requires justified machine similarity rather than assuming exchangeability [f8285, f10582, f7027, f14451].
